extracted.intended_audience: patent researchers, historians, librarians, and patent office staff
extracted.subtask_description: Extracting and interpreting bibliographic/index fields from the United States Patent Office annual alphabetical list of patentees (year 1877). The page is a structured index giving patentee, residence, invention title, dates, and cross-reference notes used for cataloguing or historical research.

rubrics_metrics.name: Name, residence, and invention
rubrics_metrics.description: Main bibliographic line combining patentee name, place of residence, and a short title/description of the invention (header: 'Name, residence, and invention.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Entries are formatted like 'Shinn, John, Philadelphia, Pa. Harness-motion for looms'. The patentee name may be followed immediately by residence and then a terse invention title. This is the primary record line to identify the inventor and the invention.

rubrics_metrics.name: Date
rubrics_metrics.description: Issue date of the patent shown in abbreviated month/day/year form (column header: 'Date.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dates appear as abbreviations such as 'Apr. 24, 1877', 'Dec. 11, 1877', or just month and year. Use this to determine the patent grant date and chronological ordering.

rubrics_metrics.name: Monthly volume
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference to the Patent Office Monthly volume or internal monthly numbering (column header: 'Monthly volume.').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric values (e.g., '1129', '843', '1004') indicate the Monthly volume/page or internal monthly reference used in the Office's indexing; may be used to locate fuller monthly-entry details.

rubrics_metrics.name: Official Gazette
rubrics_metrics.description: Reference column labelled 'Official Gazette.' giving the Official Gazette page or entry number associated with the patent.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Numeric codes (e.g., '290', '391', '1103') correspond to the Official Gazette issue/page where the patent is recorded; useful for cross-checking or retrieving the Gazette notice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Patent Number (No.)
rubrics_metrics.description: The patent number column (header 'No.') containing the official patent numbers assigned (e.g., '192,023', '193,044').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Primary unique identifier for the patent. Use to retrieve the full patent document. Numbers include commas and correspond to issued patent sequence for 1877.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assignor / Ownership-transfer notation
rubrics_metrics.description: Inline ownership-transfer notes appended to entries (phrases like 'assignor to', 'assignor of one-half interest to', 'assignor, by mesne assignments, to').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These indicate assignment of rights or partial interests and often identify assignees and fractions of interest. Example: 'Shiphertl, William C, assignor of two-thirds interest to J. J. Brooks and S. K. Davis'. Important for tracing current or historical ownership.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reissue indicator
rubrics_metrics.description: Explicit labeling of entries as reissued patents using the parenthetical 'Reissue.' or '(Reissue)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Marks patents that have been reissued rather than originally issued. Example: many entries include '(Reissue.)' following the invention title. Treat these records as reissued patents when cataloguing or analyzing patent status.

rubrics_metrics.name: Cross-reference notes ('See ...')
rubrics_metrics.description: Parenthetical cross-references such as '(See Musgrave, Shillington & Hanna.)' or '(See Crosby, Robert H., assignor)'.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Used to indicate that the substantive entry or related patent information appears under a different name or entry; follow the 'See' reference to find the primary record or related invention. Important for resolving duplicate/related entries and assignee relationships.

rubrics_metrics.name: Abbreviation and shorthand tokens (e.g., 'Same')
rubrics_metrics.description: Use of shorthand tokens like 'Same' to indicate repetition of residence, invention, or other fields from the immediately preceding entry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When 'Same' appears, it denotes that one or more fields (residence, invention, etc.) are identical to the prior line; parsing/indexing must expand or infer the repeated values from context.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ordering/Grouping (Alphabetical list)
rubrics_metrics.description: Overall organizational rule: entries are presented as an 'Alphabetical list of patentees for the year 1877' and grouped/continued across pages.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The list is alphabetized by patentee surname and continued across pages. This ordering is the primary sort key for navigation and lookup in the printed index; entries are grouped by initial letters and continued headings note continuation.
